text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London slipped to session lows during late afternoon trade and finished with losses across the board. Traders said the market was unable to sustain the mid afternoon mini-bounce and subsequently reverted to the downside. The downward trend reflected the large deliveries that took place in London against the expiring May futures contract. It was a hefty physical delivery of nearly 90,000 tonnes of sugar from British, Dutch, German and Spanish ports.

By the close August was down $1.60 at $307.00 per tonne, while October shed $1.90 to end at $302.30 per tonne. Raw sugar futures in New York closed weaker but above lows in a technical correction to the recent climb to seven-months highs, trade sources said. Sell stops were triggered from the open, with the May contract traded below support pegged at 11.09 cents/lb, also the previous upside target.

May settled 0.18 cents/lb lower at 10.95 cents/lb, after trading from 11.10 to 10.87 cents. Most active July fell 0.16 cents/lb to 10.85 cents/lb, while the remaining months finished 0.11 to 0.05 cents/lb weaker. Nearby support was seen between 10.90 and 10.80 cents in May, and then at 10.75.

AUSTRALIA - Sugar exports in February 1997 jumped to 235,585 tonnes from 209,778 tonnes in January and also sharply up on the 160,277 tonnes exported in February 1996. This brought cumulative exports in the first three quarters of 1996/97 (June/February) up to 3.819 million tonnes compared to 3.806 million tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 4.177 million tonnes against 4.479 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Canada with 686,517 tonnes raws against 545,052 tonnes, South Korea with 615,953 tonnes against 605,695, Japan with 513,830 tonnes, down from 652,916 tonnes and Malaysia with 566,258 tonnes compared to 585,077 tonnes.

Australia continues to be a substantial white sugar exporter with shipments in June/February 1996/97 reaching 156,412 tonnes compared to 163,713 tonnes in the like period a year ago. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Indonesia with 39,629 tonnes against 26,033 tonnes, New Zealand with 42,133 tonnes, up from 12,321 tonnes and Sri Lanka with 19,500 tonnes against 5,489.

INDIA - Despite burgeoning sugar stocks Indian sugar export in 1996/97 have developed rather sluggishly so far. Exports in March 1997 reached 42,652 tonnes, raw value, sharply down from 127,586 tonnes exported in March 1996. This brought cumulative exports in the first half of 1996/97 (October/March) up to 366,841 tonnes, down from 444,272 tonnes exported in the corresponding year ago period. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 952,383 tonnes, up from 37,722 tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of destination in October/March 1996/97 were Indonesia with 131,100 tonnes whites against 180,134 tonnes, Pakistan with 70,739 tonnes against nil, Sri Lanka with 47,857 tonnes, down from 103,846 tonnes and Somalia with 25,999 tonnes against 2,000 tonnes. Sugar exports are unlikely to pick up in 1996/97 given rather low world market quotations and high Indian internal production costs.

The European Union awarded 20,000 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 43.470 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on April 16. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to April 16 reached 1,797,050 tonnes, which compares to 1,944,198 tonnes last year.
